title: Positional Encoding Field
claim: Perturbing positional encodings alone warps outputs while tokens stay coherent, showing spatial structure is governed by positional encodings.
layout: Single row, left-to-right, arrows labeled Warp/Apply/Decode/Generate, branching into two output rows
description: A single left-to-right flow. At far left is a smooth orange-to-blue gradient rectangle labeled 'Canonical 2D Grid PE'. A blue arrow labeled 'Warp' leads to a distorted version of the gradient with black holes and streaks, labeled 'Warped PE'. From it, two diagonal arrows labeled 'Apply' split to an upper portrait photo of a blonde woman, representing image tokens, and a lower gray noise image, representing noise tokens. Each then goes through a blue arrow, 'Decode' for the top and 'Generate' for the bottom. The outputs are portraits with blocky, patch-shaped shifted and warped regions, such as a distorted face with visible patch boundaries. The eye goes first to the colorful gradients, then to the fragmented faces at right.
caption: Illustration of DiT patch-level independence. When positional encodings (PEs) of image tokens or noise tokens are perturbed, the decoded or generated outputs still produce semantically meaningful images. The resulting structures follow the warping imposed by the PE modification, while boundaries between patches remain visually distinct.
abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have emerged as the dominant architecture for visual generation, powering state-of-the-art image and video models. By representing images as patch tokens with positional encodings (PEs), DiTs combine Transformer scalability with spatial and temporal inductive biases. In this work, we revisit how DiTs organize visual content and discover that patch tokens exhibit a surprising degree of independence: even when PEs are perturbed, DiTs still produce globally coherent outputs, indicating that spatial coherence is primarily governed by PEs. Motivated by this finding, we introduce the Positional Encoding Field (PE-Field), which extends positional encodings from the 2D plane to a structured 3D field. PE-Field incorporates depth-aware encodings for volumetric reasoning and hierarchical encodings for fine-grained sub-patch control, enabling DiTs to model geometry directly in 3D space. Our PE-Field-augmented DiT achieves state-of-the-art performance on single-image novel view synthesis and generalizes to controllable spatial image editing.
